adjudication_records.issue_text: Mixins.scss (~102, ~108) mixes 2009 old-flexbox spec properties (`display: -webkit-box`, `-moz-box`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`) with modern 2012-spec properties in the same rule, so legacy browsers honoring the old prefixed properties get invalid modern-spec values while modern-only reordering like `margin-left: auto` silently fails, breaking the header reordering on exactly the legacy browsers the prefixes were meant to support

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add flexbox mixins in `mixins.scss` that include both 2009-era prefixed declarations (`display: -webkit-box`, `-moz-box`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`) and modern ones (`display: flex`, `order`, `align-items`). But the finding’s specific claim that legacy browsers will get “invalid modern-spec values” is not supported by what’s in the diff: the values passed in the shown usages are `center`, `baseline`, and numeric order `3`, which are valid for the old properties (`-webkit-box-align: center|baseline`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3`). The further claim that this definitively “breaks the header reordering” on legacy browsers is also not verifiable from the diff alone (it depends on actual legacy flexbox behavior, not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-post.scss (~264): `.small-action` switched to flexbox via `@include flexbox()` but `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc` sizes/offsets were tuned for block layout — replacing `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` with `padding: 0 1.5%` deletes the avatar-clearing 4em padding without re-adding horizontal separation, causing text to collapse under the avatar on narrow viewports

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `.small-action` becoming a flex container and `.small-action-desc` changing from `padding: ... 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but nothing in the shown changes demonstrates that the text will “collapse under the avatar” (i.e., overlap). In a flex layout, siblings typically lay out side-by-side without needing a left-clearing padding, and the diff does not show `.topic-avatar` being positioned/overlaid in a way that would cause collapse. The claimed narrow-viewport overlap is therefore not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy 2009 box-align prefixes (-webkit-box-align, -moz-box-align) don't support the 'baseline' value used by badges.css.scss, causing old WebKit browsers to fall back to stretch and misalign badges

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `align-items($alignment)` mixin that sets `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` and then uses `@include align-items(baseline);` in `badges.css.scss`. However, the finding claims use of both `-webkit-box-align` and `-moz-box-align`; the mixin does not set `-moz-box-align` at all. Also, whether old WebKit’s `-webkit-box-align` supports `baseline` cannot be verified from the diff itself (it’s a browser-compat claim not evidenced by code behavior here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: -ms-align-items is not a valid property in any browser; IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, so this fabricated syntax may be cargo-culted by future maintainers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The latter is indeed a nonstandard/invalid property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), so the finding is grounded in the added code. It likely won’t break layout (it will just be ignored), but it adds misleading/cargo-culted CSS that could confuse future maintainers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 2009/2012 vendor prefix stack in all four mixins is dead code with no supported-browser floor or verification, incurring maintenance cost without acceptance criteria

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add four new flexbox-related mixins with a wide set of legacy vendor-prefixed properties (e.g., `display: -webkit-box;`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, `-ms-flex-order`). However, the finding asserts these prefixes are "dead code" for 2009/2012 specs and that there is "no supported-browser floor or verification"—neither browser support requirements nor acceptance criteria are present in the diff, so it’s not verifiable from the change itself whether these prefixes are unnecessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Making .contents a flex container turns all direct children (e.g. .valign-helper) into flex items with flex-shrink: 1, causing .title text to shrink/truncate at narrow widths instead of wrapping

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `.contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox()`), so its direct children become flex items, but the finding’s specific claim that `.title` text will shrink/truncate instead of wrapping is not supported by anything shown here. There are no added/changed rules in the diff that enforce truncation (e.g., `white-space: nowrap`, `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, or a constrained/min-width scenario on `.title`). Also, `.title` styles are removed entirely in this hunk, so the described behavior can’t be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant dual encoding of panel positioning: margin-left: auto plus order(3) encode the same intent, creating a cross-file coupling between header.scss and topic.scss that can drift when one is updated

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.panel` now uses `margin-left: auto;` and `@include order(3);` inside a flex container (`.contents` got `@include flexbox()`). These do not encode the same intent: `order()` controls flex item ordering, while `margin-left: auto` pushes the item to the end of the main axis. Also, the claimed cross-file coupling to topic.scss is not supported by the diff: topic.scss adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper`, which is unrelated to `header.scss`’s `.panel` selector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-post.scss:277-302: unrelated visual restyling of .small-action blocks (padding, margin, paragraph margin changes) not traceable to any stated requirement, bundled into a performance PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic-post.scss` clearly changes `.small-action` layout/styling beyond adding flex alignment: it adds `@include flexbox()`/`align-items(center)`, changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` plus `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, changes nested `p` margin from `5px 0` to `0`, and removes `padding-top: 4px` on `> p`. These are substantive visual restyling changes, not just mechanical refactoring, and could be considered scope creep if the PR’s intent was unrelated (though the PR purpose isn’t verifiable from the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: badges.css.scss:55-58: converting .badge-wrapper.bullet from native flex to legacy-prefix mixins is unnecessary churn with no requirement, adding old-IE prefixes and expanding maintenance surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.badge-wrapper.bullet` from native `inline-flex`/`align-items` to `@include inline-flex()` and `@include align-items(baseline)` and adds mixins with legacy-prefixed declarations. However, the claim that this is "unnecessary churn" or that there is "no requirement" cannot be verified from the diff alone; it's an arguable style/maintainability preference rather than a concrete, diff-provable issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.scss:30-35: line-height addition and .bullet margin-top removal in .extra-info-wrapper are unrelated visual changes with no justification

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `.extra-info-wrapper` gaining `line-height: 1.5;` and removing the nested `.badge-wrapper &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }`. However, the finding’s claim that these are “unrelated” changes with “no justification” is subjective and cannot be verified from the diff alone (they could be part of the broader flexbox/alignment refactor).

adjudication_records.issue_text: order(3) on .panel (header.scss) and order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss) create a cross-file implicit ordering contract with no single source of truth; edits to one file can break visual ordering with no test signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@include order(3)` for `.panel` in `header.scss` and `@include order(2)` for `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, but these selectors are in different components/layouts and the diff shows no shared flex container or shared ordering scheme between them. Flex `order` only affects sibling items within the same flex formatting context; nothing in the diff establishes a cross-file contract between header and topic styles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss:20: .title float removed without an explicit order/flex replacement, leaving title ordering implicit and dependent on DOM source order

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss` the `.title` float is removed, but `.contents` is converted into a flex container via `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`, and `.panel` is pushed to the right with `margin-left: auto` plus an explicit `@include order(3)`. The diff does not show a broken layout or missing flex replacement; leaving `.title` at default flex order (DOM order) is normal and not verifiably a defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:96-131: vendored mixins include speculative unused members failing the deletion test

adjudication.rationale: The added mixins in mixins.scss (flexbox, inline-flex, align-items, order) are directly used in the same diff: header.scss uses flexbox/align-items/order, topic-post.scss uses flexbox/align-items, topic.scss uses order, and badges.css.scss uses inline-flex/align-items. The claim that they are “speculative unused members” is not supported by the shown changes, and “failing the deletion test” references external context not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins include dead-wrong -ms-align-items property which is not real (correct name is -ms-flex-align), shipping dead CSS to every IE user

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss, the new @mixin align-items($alignment) includes both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` (the real IE10/11 property) and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (a non-existent/unsupported property). This is verifiable from the diff and would emit useless CSS, but it’s unlikely to cause broken behavior because unknown CSS properties are ignored by browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of float declarations from .title/.panel in header.scss breaks header layout (title and panel stack full-width) in non-flexbox browsers like IE9 and older Android that the vendor prefixes target; floats should be kept as a fallback

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }` are removed and `.contents` is converted to flex via `@include flexbox()` with `.panel { margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }`. If a browser doesn’t support any of the emitted flexbox syntaxes, the elements will fall back to normal block layout and could stack. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish that IE9/other non-flexbox browsers are within the project’s supported matrix (and the new mixins target various flexbox implementations rather than floats), so it’s a compatibility/fallback concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items mixin maps 'baseline' through to -webkit-box-align, which is invalid in old flexbox, causing old-WebKit browsers to fall back to stretch while modern browsers get baseline (inconsistent vertical alignment of category badge)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `align-items($alignment)` mixin that forwards the same value to several vendor properties, including `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;`. The finding claims `baseline` is invalid for `-webkit-box-align` and would fall back to `stretch`, but the diff itself does not demonstrate that, and `baseline` is a recognized value for the legacy `-webkit-box-align` property in the old flexbox syntax. Nothing in the changed SCSS indicates an inherent inconsistency/bug solely from mapping `baseline` through this mixin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order mixin maps CSS order values 1:1 to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, but the old-box spec is 1-based, making ordering of header children (.title 0, .extra-info 2, .panel 3) undefined in old-WebKit/Firefox browsers
matched_golden_ids: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based and that directly mapping CSS order values (including 0) causes incorrect/undefined ordering in old WebKit/Firefox, which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action loses its float/padding-based avatar gutter in non-flex browsers, causing text to overlap/abut the avatar with no gutter since the old fallback was deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old left padding on `.small-action-desc` (from `padding: ... 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%`) and adds flexbox via `@include flexbox()`, but the claim about a lost float-based fallback causing text to overlap the avatar in non-flex browsers is not verifiable from the shown changes: there is no float on `.small-action .topic-avatar` in the diff context, and nothing in the diff demonstrates an existing non-flex layout that would overlap/abut without that padding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: margin-left: auto for right-aligning .panel does not work in IE10's -ms-flexbox implementation; it requires -ms-flex-pack: end instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.contents` to a flex container and right-aligns `.panel` via `margin-left: auto;` while also adding `-ms-flexbox` vendor support in the `flexbox()` mixin. If IE10’s `-ms-flexbox` implementation doesn’t honor auto margins for flex item alignment (as the finding claims), `.panel` would no longer right-align there, i.e., a real behavior regression tied to this change. However, the diff alone can’t confirm IE10’s runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action-desc padding/margin rewrite (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top 5px → 0 1.5%) silently changes visual layout, replacing fixed avatar-relative indent with viewport-relative indent at all viewport widths

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;` (in `topic-post.scss`), which will alter spacing/indent behavior (fixed `4em` left indent and top margin removed). However, the claim that it becomes “viewport-relative” is not strictly grounded (percent padding is relative to the containing block’s width, not necessarily the viewport). This is a real, reviewable layout change but not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting p { margin: 5px 0 } and padding-top: 4px inside .small-action-desc/.extra-info-wrapper removes deliberate vertical rhythm spacing unrelated to the flexbox conversion

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change spacing in `topic-post.scss` by setting `.small-action-desc .action-desc p { margin: 0; }` (was `5px 0`) and removing `.small-action-desc > p { padding-top: 4px; }`. However, the finding’s claim that this spacing was “deliberate” and “unrelated to the flexbox conversion” is not verifiable from the diff, and it incorrectly ties the `padding-top: 4px` removal to `.extra-info-wrapper` (that block changes `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }`, not padding-top).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } from .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper changes vertical alignment of bullet category badges and may regress on legacy-prefixed flexbox engines with different baseline behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }`, which could change the visual vertical alignment of bullet-style badges in that context. However, the claim about regressions on legacy prefixed flexbox baseline behavior isn’t directly supported by this specific selector change (the `.badge-wrapper` here is still `float: left`, and no flex container is shown around it in this diff). So it’s a plausible UI-regression concern, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded flexbox order values for .panel and .extra-info-wrapper couple visual order to DOM source order, breaking the previous float layout's decoupling if the panel precedes extra-info in the DOM

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit flexbox ordering via `@include order(3);` on `.panel` (header.scss) and `@include order(2);` on `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss). These are hard-coded numeric “magic” values that make layout ordering dependent on a shared ordering scheme across sibling elements, which can be fragile/maintenance-heavy compared to the previous float-based approach. However, the claim that this definitively “breaks” behavior based on actual DOM ordering can’t be fully verified from this diff alone (we don’t see the HTML or all sibling order rules).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New align-items/order mixins emit -ms-align-items (not a real IE10 property) and lack -moz-box-align/-moz-box-orient, so align-items(center) silently does nothing on 2009-spec engines the prefixed output claims to support

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss, @mixin flexbox() emits `display: -moz-box;` (2009 flexbox spec), but @mixin align-items($alignment) does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`, so alignment won’t apply on engines using the `-moz-box` model. The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a standard IE10 property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is present), indicating incorrect/ineffective prefixed output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real IE10 old-spec property (correct mapping is -ms-flex-align, which the mixin also emits)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` which emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The finding is correct that `-ms-align-items` is not part of the IE10/old flexbox spec, while `-ms-flex-align` is the proper mapping and is already present. This is a real, diff-grounded issue (an unnecessary/invalid vendor property) but it’s unlikely to cause broken behavior since invalid properties are ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flexbox mixin's -moz-box/-webkit-box display values pair with the old box model while order maps -webkit-box-ordinal-group to the new-spec integer, causing old-WebKit implementations to mis-order (old syntax is 1-based group, not 0-based index)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a flexbox compatibility mixin that includes legacy `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` while the new `@mixin order($val)` sets `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val` directly. In the legacy box model, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is effectively 1-based (default 1), whereas modern `order` is 0-based (default 0). With usages like `@include order(2)` and `@include order(3)` added in this diff, old WebKit implementations that fall back to `-webkit-box` can end up with an off-by-one ordering compared to the intended modern flex ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:120 align-items mixin emits -moz-box-align with modern flexbox keyword values (center, baseline) though -moz-box-* was never shipped in release Firefox and the display:-moz-box context isn't consistently provided

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but it does not emit any `-moz-box-align`. Therefore the finding’s claim about `-moz-box-*` output is not supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -moz-inline-box at mixins.scss:110 is not a valid value

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `inline-flex()` mixin containing `display: -moz-inline-box;` (mixins.scss). The finding asserts this is “not a valid value,” but from the diff alone there’s no verifiable defect: it’s a vendor-prefixed fallback in a list of `display` declarations and would simply be ignored by browsers that don’t support it. The claim about invalidity is not provable from the patch and is likely a standards/pedantry assertion rather than a concrete bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:121 -ms-align-items is a non-existent property; only -ms-flex-align is valid, making the claimed cross-browser coverage illusory and producing dead/invalid CSS for old Android/IE10 consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` and it includes `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` alongside `-ms-flex-align`. The presence of `-ms-align-items` is verifiably in the diff and is not a standard/commonly supported MS flexbox property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`). This makes that declaration dead/invalid CSS and undermines the intended cross-browser vendor coverage, but it’s unlikely to cause broken behavior (the valid `-ms-flex-align` and unprefixed `align-items` remain).
